The name use-sync-external-store-shim imitates `use-sync-external-store/shim`, the shim entry point of React's use-sync-external-store package; the npm account djdhhdjdjf7777 registered the name again on 2026-11-24, after its 2023 versions had been removed, and published 2.0.0 and 2.2.0, which have no functional code. Each has a postinstall script that runs `node index.js` on npm install, which POSTs a JSON beacon (`event: "authorized-poc-test"`, a random test id, `status: "executed"`) to `https://webhook.site/0a4d6535-e2dd-46b7-aff7-8af65c145c50` (2.0.0) or `https://webhook.site/b4ea4473-01d9-4763-9e39-3b02063219d5` (2.2.0), telling the collector the package was installed and from which network. The same account published the same beacon as bundle-entry-points, paystation-embed-app and global-error-handling.

## Source: amazon-inspector (f580338454159b608f80b985909f20a4e4fafa8b3f4eba644c5ea82e4e5c1d29)
Package name impersonates the legitimate `use-sync-external-store` React shim while its `package.json` description ('A utility for managing SVG buckets') is unrelated to that purpose. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` hook running `node index.js`, which reads `os.hostname()` and `process.cwd()` and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded webhook at `https://webhook.site/0a4d6535-e2dd-46b7-aff7-8af65c145c50`. The exfiltration fires automatically during `npm install` without any user interaction and sends installer host identifiers to an attacker-controlled collector. The shape — misleading name, mismatched description, install-time beacon to an anonymous webhook endpoint — is the recon/confirmation stage of a typosquat supply-chain attack.
